MAJOR: `design_contract_check.enforced()` returns True whenever `item.design_pack` is present, ignoring `enforce_from`; because gate1/gate2 now call it, every in-flight legacy item that already has a pack is retroactively forced to satisfy `controls`, `guideline_coverage`, `review_scope`, `coverage` and hard-fails Gate 1/2 — contradicting the stated "migration is explicit" risk mitigation.

`architect_review._build_prompt` (diff mode) unconditionally concatenates `_design_body(item)` outside any try/except (unlike the guardrails block); a missing/unreadable `engineering/design/<ID>.md` aborts prompt construction, so Gate 2.5 cannot run at all for any item lacking a generated design file.

`design_contract_check._test_exists` returns True for any string starting with `go test`/`python -m pytest`/`pytest ` and `_evidence_exists` returns True for any string containing `://`, so a design can satisfy the "real failing test / evidence" contract with a nonexistent command or an arbitrary URL.

`config/ci-cd-gates.json` and `precheck.py` register `scripts/dev/delivery_completeness_check.py`, which is neither added in this candidate nor listed in `pf_process_check.FILES`; the new blocking gate has no existence/import self-check, so a missing or broken script fails precheck for every run with no framework-level diagnosis.
MINOR: `architect_review._build_prompt` raises the diff body cap 180k→500k chars with no token/cost bound; a large candidate now yields one very large provider call, removing the previous prompt-size guardrail silently.

The diff-mode guardrails injection is wrapped in `except Exception: pass`, so a broken `design_guardrails` module silently drops CL-009 delivery-learnings injection with no stderr event, unlike other fail-closed paths in the same function.

`test-framework/tests/conftest.py` sets `PF_BACKLOG_DB=off` autouse for the whole suite; DB-path behaviour is now default-off globally, so regressions that only appear in DB mode can pass green unless a test explicitly opts in.

`worktree_fingerprint` hashes only HEAD, symbolic-ref, `refs/heads` and `ls-files -s` (index); a test that rewrites a tracked file's content without staging is undetected, contrary to its "abort when a test mutates the worktree" docstring.

`framework_ref_check` regex-matches raw added lines under `core/`, `api/`, `adapters/`, `go/`, so neutral comments/docstrings naming `opencode`/`dashboard` (e.g. "not coupled to OpenCode") fail the blocking gate; comments are indistinguishable from imports.

`self_review_check.changed_lines` scans only `merge-base..HEAD`, so uncommitted worktree placeholders/TODOs pass the blocking `--strict` precheck, while the encoding gate deliberately covers worktree/untracked files — inconsistent change-set definitions.

`control_runner` writes control output as `engineering/trails/<item>-<ctl>.txt` by default, mixing non-JSON artifacts into the trail directory that other checks enumerate and schema-validate as trail JSON.

`config/store-registry.json` adds `config/*.yml` to the blanket pattern list; every future YAML config is excluded from registry enforcement, weakening the store-registry gate for the exact class of files this item is adding (`pf-gates.yml`).

`control_gate`/`control_runner` validate `check` prefixes by raw `startswith` on the string while `control_runner` executes via `shlex.split`, so a check like `go testfoo` passes the gate but is rejected at execution (or vice versa for quoting) — two parsers for one contract.
NIT: `design_contract_check._placeholder` is defined but never called (`problems` uses `_token_in` directly), leaving dead duplicate logic in a fail-closed validator.

`gate2_completion_check` reuses `ledger_bad` across a `for/else` and a post-loop `if`, which reads as an intentional fallthrough; a reader cannot tell whether the empty-list `else` branch is load-bearing.
`biis_tier_check --apply` persists a generic `tier_reasons` string that discards the matched pattern, so an applied tier cannot later be audited against the surface that produced it.
`review_ledger.record` returns silently when a duplicate `review_sha` is seen, so callers cannot distinguish "recorded" from "no-op", and the `_ingest` failure path cannot report it.

`config/control-matrix.json` and `config/guideline-compliance.json` each restate `allowed_check_prefixes` (nearly identical lists) with no single source, so allowed-command policy can drift between the two gates.
SUMMARY: Direction is right (delta re-review, design pack, encoding gate, ownership/controls) and the docs/config scaffolding is thorough, but enforcement activation is not date-gated in practice and will retroactively block in-flight items.
Highest risk: `design_contract_check.enforced()` turning on for any item with a `design_pack`, and the unguarded `_design_body` read that can break Gate 2.5 outright.
Evidence integrity is weakened by permissive `_test_exists`/`_evidence_exists`, and the new `delivery-completeness` blocking gate is registered without a framework self-check.
Change-set definitions (review delta, self-review, control SHA, encoding) now diverge four ways; converge them on one helper before shipping.
